headline: Lumen 3 open-source language model released under permissive licence
subheadline: The non-profit Lumen Foundation says the 40-billion-parameter model can run on a single workstation GPU.
description: The Lumen Foundation has released Lumen 3, a 40-billion-parameter open-source language model under a permissive licence, saying it can run on a single workstation GPU.
author: m-chen

image.alt: Rows of server racks with cabling inside a data centre
image.caption: Server racks in a data centre (file photo). Lumen 3 was trained on a cluster donated by three universities, the foundation says.
image.credit: Photo: Carl Lender / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

seo.title: Lumen 3 open-source AI model released under permissive licence
seo.description: Lumen Foundation releases Lumen 3, a 40B-parameter open-source language model that runs on a single workstation GPU.

body: The Lumen Foundation released the third generation of its open-source language model on Tuesday, publishing weights, training code and a detailed data statement under a permissive licence that allows commercial use.

Lumen 3 has 40 billion parameters and, according to the foundation, runs at usable speeds on a single consumer graphics card when quantised. Independent developers who received early access reported similar results.

items: A published list of every data source used in training, with licensing status.
An opt-out registry for website owners honoured during the crawl.
A model card describing known weaknesses, including weaker performance in low-resource languages.

body: The foundation said transparency about training data was a direct response to lawsuits facing commercial model developers and to forthcoming disclosure rules in several jurisdictions.

body.text: If you cannot say what your model learned from, you cannot honestly say what it is good for.

body: Researchers praised the data statement but noted that Lumen 3 still trails the largest commercial models on reasoning benchmarks. Several small businesses said the ability to run the model locally, without sending customer data to a third party, mattered more to them than benchmark scores.
Downloads passed 200,000 within the first 24 hours, the foundation said.
